chat.text: I'll be straightforward: given the payoff structure and that this is a one-shot interaction with no memory or reputation carrying forward, I'm planning to DEFECT this round. I think mutual defection is likely the rational outcome here given we can't build trust across iterations. What's your thinking?

I appreciate the candor. I agree with your analysis: since each step is effectively a standalone game with no memory, reputation, or enforcement mechanism carrying forward, cooperation can't be credibly sustained. Any agreement to cooperate would be unenforceable, and the dominant strategy in a one-shot game is to defect regardless of what the other player does. So I'll be defecting this round as well — not out of distrust of you specifically, but because it's the rational choice given the structure. No hard feelings, just optimizing for the payoff matrix as given.
Agreed — mutual defection is the rational equilibrium here given the one-shot, memoryless structure. No hard feelings on my end either, just playing the game as designed. Good luck.
Sounds good. Glad we're aligned on the reasoning here. Take care, and good luck to you too.
